title: AWS PrivateLink Pricing: Monthly Cost Guide (2026)
summary: AWS PrivateLink pricing includes hourly endpoint costs plus data transfer fees. Understand the breakdown to estimate your actual monthly expenses.
body_markdown:
## Report PrivateLink spend weekly with Activepieces


Activepieces can't replace PrivateLink or cut an endpoint's rate. A scheduled workflow can pull your AWS cost data every week and tell a named person which endpoints are costing money and which look idle.


The steps it uses are integrations in the open source repository, which counts 750 integrations under an MIT-licensed core, so you can read what each one does before you run it.


Describe the weekly report to the built-in chat and it publishes a live flow in your account, the same kind of flow a builder would assemble by hand.


That gives the owner an unowned endpoint needs: a recurring prompt, in a channel they already read, that someone has to answer.


### What the workflow does


In the screenshot below, the flow is titled "Test Flow" in the Activepieces builder and is a general-purpose template rather than a PrivateLink-specific one.


It starts with a schedule trigger and passes through Google Sheets, a loop, a date helper, an HTTP request, two AI steps and a Sheets insert, so any single step failure blocks the entire workflow.


After that comes a router with a "Branch 1" and an "Otherwise" path, then a Gmail send step.


Read it as a shape to adapt: every step is a box you can swap for the one your reporting needs.


For this problem, the schedule trigger fires weekly. The HTTP request calls the AWS Cost Explorer API, filtered to VPC endpoint usage, and the loop walks through each result.


The date helper sets the reporting window, and the Sheets insert keeps a running record, so you can see whether an endpoint's cost is growing or flat.


The router then separates endpoints with meaningful spend from those showing little or no traffic, and the last step sends each group to its owner by email or Slack.


Because the output lands in a sheet, the history becomes evidence when you argue for consolidating endpoints.


Each weekly run also leaves a run trace in your Activepieces account, so when a figure in the report looks wrong you can open that run and read what happened step by step.


### What the PrivateLink spend workflow does not do


It doesn't delete, resize or merge anything. Removing an endpoint stays a human decision, which is the right place for it, since a quiet endpoint may serve a monthly job.


Whatever Cost Explorer reports is all it sees. Cost data arrives with a delay, so a freshly created endpoint can run for a while before it appears. And a low-traffic flag is a prompt to investigate, not proof the endpoint is unused.


You must supply the AWS credentials and the filters yourself, and the owner mapping lives in your sheet, so it's only as accurate as you keep it.
